intro.title: useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useFetch` that simplifies fetching data from an API. You will learn how to encapsulate the logic for making HTTP requests, handling loading states, and managing errors into a reusable function. The core programming concepts involved are React hooks, specifically `useState` and `useEffect`, and asynchronous JavaScript using `async/await` or Promises. You'll use TypeScript to define types for the data, loading state, and error, ensuring type safety throughout your component. By the end, you'll have a handy hook that can be used in any component to fetch data with clean and maintainable code.
intro.usecase: The useFetch pattern is essential for loading dynamic data in modern web applications. You'll see this pattern in dashboard widgets that display real-time metrics, e-commerce product listings with filtering, and social media feeds that load new content as users scroll. Developers implement useFetch whenever they need to retrieve API data while managing loading states, errors, and caching. This approach keeps UI components clean by separating data-fetching logic from presentation.
